climate.overview_html: The Pacific Pre-COP in Fiji and Tuvalu concludes 8 October; a Nadi Declaration is expected to formalize Pacific nations’ call for the ocean-climate nexus and 1.5°C to anchor COP31. The IPCC AR7 timeline remains in deadlock ahead of the IPCC-65 plenary (12–16 October, Addis Ababa), with developed countries and SIDS/LDCs clashing over whether all three flagship reports clear by July–September 2028 or WG II and III are pushed to mid-2029 — while the Secretariat warns the trust fund runs dry by end-2028 without increased contributions. In a landmark step for emerging-market carbon pricing, India’s first Carbon Credit Certificates (CCCs) are being issued this month under the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, covering ~490 obligated entities, with trading expected to begin in November.

items.headline: IPCC-65 Plenary Opens 12 October in Addis Ababa: AR7 Timeline in Deadlock; Developed Country vs. SIDS/LDC Positions Two Years Apart; Secretariat Warns Trust Fund Exhausted by End-2028 Without New Contributions
items.summary: The IPCC's 65th Plenary session opens 12 October 2026 in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, with the primary agenda item being agreement on a delivery timeline for the AR7 set of assessment reports. A large coalition of developed countries, SIDS, and progressive Latin American states presses for all three Working Group reports to be approved by July–September 2028, so they feed into the UNFCCC's 2028 Global Stocktake. A separate bloc argues this timetable is unworkable, pushing WG2 and WG3 approvals to mid-2029. Complicating negotiations, the IPCC Secretariat has warned that the panel's trust fund will run out of cash by end-2028 without a significant increase in contributions — potentially jeopardising delivery of the AR7 Synthesis Report before the 2030 climate deadline.

items.source: Outlook Business / Carbon Pulse / BEE India
items.headline: India Launches First Carbon Credit Certificates (CCCs) Under CCTS October 2026; ~490 Obligated Entities Across Nine Industrial Sectors; Trading Expected November 2026–January 2027
items.summary: India's Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) has begun issuing Carbon Credit Certificates (CCCs) under the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS) in October 2026, completing the FY26 compliance cycle — targets ran through 31 March, four months for verification through July, three months for assessment and CCC issuance through October. Approximately 490 obligated entities across nine industrial sectors including cement, aluminium, chlor-alkali, paper, petrochemicals, textiles, rubber and pulp now hold binding emission intensity targets. Compliance-based CCC trading is expected to commence on the Indian Energy Exchange (IEX) in November 2026, with the first window running through January 2027. India thus becomes the second major emerging-market economy after China to operationalise a compliance carbon market at national scale.

items.headline: Pre-COP Fiji and Tuvalu (5–8 October): Pacific Leaders Press for 1.5°C Commitment, Ocean-Climate Nexus Integration in COP31 Agenda; $310–365 Billion Annual Adaptation Finance Gap; 50+ Countries Represented
items.summary: More than 50 countries gathered in Nadi, Fiji for the Pacific Pre-COP (5–8 October 2026), co-hosted by Fiji, Tuvalu and Australia, to set the agenda for COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye in November. Forum included on-site visits to Tuvalu to document sea-level rise affecting permanent residents. Fiji's climate minister outlined three priorities: keeping 1.5°C within reach, ensuring climate finance reaches vulnerable communities, and giving the ocean its rightful place in the international climate regime. A UN report found developing countries need $310–$365 billion annually for adaptation while receiving only $26 billion in 2023. A draft COP31 presidency text on ocean protections circulated at Pre-COP — the first time ocean warming and acidification are proposed as a standalone agenda item at a UNFCCC conference.

items.source: Washington Post / NBC News / Claims Journal
items.headline: US Supreme Court Hears Boulder, Colorado Climate Liability Case Against ExxonMobil and Suncor; Ruling Could Determine Fate of Dozens of State and Local Government Climate Lawsuits; Justices Appear ‘Stumped’
items.summary: The US Supreme Court heard oral arguments on October 5, 2026 in a case where Boulder, Colorado seeks to hold ExxonMobil and Suncor Energy liable for climate change damages and for allegedly misleading the public about fossil fuels' climate risks. The oil companies seek to remove the case to federal court, where liability claims face a higher dismissal bar. The case's outcome will determine whether dozens of similar lawsuits by states, cities and counties — involving San Francisco, New York City, Hawaii and others — can proceed in state courts. NBC News reported the justices appeared 'stumped' by the procedural complexities.

items.headline: Super El Niño Kelvin Waves Raising US West Coast Sea Levels 15–30 cm; Erosion and Flooding Risk From California to Alaska Through February; Waves Moving North at 150 Miles Per Day
items.summary: A series of oceanic Kelvin waves tied to the 2026 Super El Niño began striking the US Pacific coast in early October, raising sea levels 15–30 cm along the California shoreline and moving north at approximately 150 miles per day toward Oregon, Washington, and Alaska. The surge is expected to continue through February, combining with above-average North Pacific swell and larger-than-average spring tides to create compounded erosion and coastal flooding risk.

items.headline: Swiss Glaciers Lose 5.5% of Ice Volume in 2026 — Second-Worst Annual Melt on Record; Aletsch Sets Record Since 1870; 20% Volume Lost Since 2021
items.summary: Swiss glaciers lost 5.5% of their total ice volume in 2026, the second-largest annual ice loss in the instrumental record after 5.9% in 2022. The record-breaking European heatwave of summer 2026 combined with an unusually snow-poor winter to accelerate melting. The Aletsch Glacier recorded its biggest annual melt since systematic monitoring began in 1870. Over five years (2021–2026), Switzerland has lost nearly 20% of its total glacier ice volume.

items.headline: Copernicus Ocean State Report 10: Mediterranean Hits Two-Decade High in Marine Heatwave Days; Arctic Ice Declining 490,000 km²/Decade; Black Sea and Mediterranean +4.6°C Peak Marine Heatwave Intensity; Ocean Heat Content Record in 2025
items.summary: The Copernicus Marine Service's 10th Ocean State Report (OSR10) found the Mediterranean Sea recorded its highest number of marine heatwave days in the 20-year record; the Black Sea and Mediterranean experienced peak marine heatwave intensity more than 4.6°C above normal in 2024; Arctic sea ice is declining at nearly 490,000 km² per decade; Mediterranean SSTs rose at 0.32°C per decade from 1982–2024; and global ocean heat content reached its highest level on record in 2025.

major_events.name: Hurricane Isaias — NAMED STORM; GULF OF MEXICO; CATEGORY 1–2 HURRICANE LANDFALL FRIDAY–SATURDAY
major_events.status: ACTIVE — Tropical Depression Nine was designated in the southwestern Gulf of Mexico on 6 October and named Tropical Storm Isaias on 7 October 2026; NHC forecast projects rapid intensification over anomalously warm Gulf SSTs to Category 1–2 hurricane before landfall Friday night through Saturday; track cone spans Louisiana to the Florida Panhandle; Yale Climate Connections notes rising Gulf hurricane landfall odds
major_events.impact: Hurricane watches and warnings expected by Thursday; heavy rainfall 6–12 inches and storm surge 3–6 feet in landfall zone; flash flooding risk inland across Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, the Florida Panhandle and southern Georgia; first hurricane landfall of the 2026 Atlantic season

major_events.name: Typhoon Koguma (JTWC 28W) — INTENSIFYING; 15.3°N, 164.0°E; TYPHOON STATUS EXPECTED THURSDAY
major_events.status: ACTIVE — As of 7 October 00:00 UTC, Koguma is at 15.3°N, 164.0°E with sustained winds of 93 km/h (50 kt) and central pressure 996 mb, moving northwest at 20 km/h; JTWC 5-day forecast projects intensification to 105 kt (121 mph); recurvature east of Japan by day 7; Super Typhoon potential if 105 kt forecast verifies
major_events.impact: Growing swell and seas across central Marshall Islands; typhoon intensity expected Thursday–Friday; deep warm western Pacific water anomalies from the Super El Niño providing exceptional intensification potential; would be the fourth Super Typhoon of the 2026 season if JTWC forecast verifies

major_events.name: Typhoon Nolo (formerly Hurricane Nolo) — WEAKENING; POST-TROPICAL TRANSITION; OPEN WESTERN PACIFIC
major_events.status: WEAKENING — As of 6 October, Nolo has weakened to 100 mph (87 kt) and is located approximately 719 km south-southeast of Wake Island; post-tropical or extratropical transition underway; no land threats
major_events.impact: Diminishing swells across the central and western North Pacific; no land warnings or watches in effect

major_events.name: Southeast Asian Haze — ONGOING; Indonesia Peat Fires; ASEAN Alert Level 3
major_events.status: ACTIVE — ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre Alert Level 3 remains in effect; Indonesia’s 2026 fire season (worst in 11 years) continues driving transboundary haze across Sumatra, Kalimantan and peninsular Southeast Asia; Super El Niño drought sustaining peat fire conditions
major_events.impact: More than 12 million people under hazardous air quality; school closures in Malaysia and Singapore

weather.overview_html: The Gulf of Mexico has rapidly become the primary tropical threat for the US: Tropical Depression Nine formed in the southwestern Gulf on October 6 and was named Tropical Storm Isaias on October 7, with NHC forecast models projecting rapid intensification to a Category 1–2 hurricane before Gulf Coast landfall Friday night through Saturday — what would be the first hurricane landfall of the 2026 Atlantic season. In the western Pacific, Typhoon Koguma (28W) is actively intensifying at 15.3°N, 164.0°E with JTWC forecasting 105 kt within five days; Typhoon Nolo is weakening into post-tropical status west of Wake Island. The Southeast Asian peat-fire haze remains at ASEAN Alert Level 3 with 12 million people under hazardous air quality.

items.headline: Tropical Storm Isaias Named in Gulf of Mexico; NHC Forecast: Category 1–2 Hurricane at Gulf Coast Landfall Friday–Saturday; Louisiana to Florida Panhandle; First Hurricane Landfall of 2026 Atlantic Season
items.summary: Tropical Depression Nine formed in the southwestern Gulf of Mexico on October 6, 2026, and was upgraded to Tropical Storm Isaias on October 7. The National Hurricane Center's forecast projects rapid intensification over anomalously warm Gulf of Mexico SSTs — running 1–2°C above normal due to the 2026 Super El Niño — with landfall as a Category 1–2 hurricane expected Friday night through Saturday. The track cone spans from Louisiana to the Florida Panhandle. Heavy rainfall of 6–12 inches, storm surge of 3–6 feet, and high winds are forecast in the landfall zone, with inland flooding risk extending through the Southeast. Isaias would be the ninth named storm of the 2026 Atlantic season and the first hurricane landfall on the US mainland.

items.headline: Typhoon Koguma (28W) Intensifying at 15.3°N, 164.0°E with 93 km/h Winds; JTWC Forecasts 105 kt in 5 Days; Typhoon Status Thursday; Super Typhoon Potential; Track Points East of Japan
items.summary: Typhoon Koguma (JTWC 28W) is actively intensifying as of October 7, 2026, at 15.3°N, 164.0°E, moving northwest at 20 km/h with maximum sustained winds of 93 km/h (50 kt) and central pressure at 996 mb. JTWC's five-day forecast projects intensification to 105 kt (121 mph) — Super Typhoon threshold. Typhoon status is expected by Thursday–Friday. The seven-day track shows recurvature northeastward east of Japan, with large model spread beyond day 5. The 2026 Super El Niño's anomalously warm western Pacific Ocean temperatures are providing exceptional intensification potential, consistent with the season's record proportion of Super Typhoons.

items.headline: Hurricane Nolo Crosses International Date Line and Becomes Typhoon Nolo — Only Second Dateline-Crossing Storm Since Hurricane Dora (2023); Now Weakening West of Wake Island
items.summary: Hurricane Nolo crossed the International Date Line on October 4, 2026 and was reclassified by JTWC as Typhoon Nolo — only the second storm to complete this Pacific basin-crossing transition since Hurricane Dora in 2023. Peak intensity was approximately 155 mph (135 kt). As of October 6, the storm has weakened to 100 mph (87 kt) and is located approximately 719 km south-southeast of Wake Island, with post-tropical/extratropical transition now underway. No land threats remain.

items.headline: DANA Cold-Drop Flash Flooding Kills One, Prompts 90 Rescues in Eastern Spain; 140 mm Rain in 2 Hours at Madrigueras, Albacete; Four Homes Collapse; Valencia and Catalonia Also Hit
items.summary: A DANA (Depresión Aislada en Niveles Altos, cut-off low) system struck Eastern Spain overnight on October 2–3, 2026, dropping more than 140 mm of rain in approximately two hours at Madrigueras, Albacete. The flash flood killed one person (a 102-year-old woman) and prompted rescue of approximately 90 residents. Four homes collapsed and more than 150 vehicles were submerged. Southern France issued red alerts for Hérault and Gard departments simultaneously. Mediterranean autumn DANA events have intensified as warmer SSTs provide greater moisture loading.

items.headline: 2026 Southeast Asian Haze: Indonesia’s Worst Wildfire Season in 11 Years; ASEAN Alert Level 3 Active; 12 Million People Under Hazardous Air Quality; Super El Niño Drought Fuels Peat Fires
items.summary: The ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre's Alert Level 3 — the highest tier in its haze warning system — remains active as Indonesia's 2026 wildfire season, its worst in 11 years, sustains transboundary haze across Sumatra, Kalimantan and peninsular Southeast Asia. More than 12 million people face hazardous air quality. School closures continue in parts of Malaysia and Singapore. The Super El Niño is sustaining the crisis through drought conditions across Sumatra and Kalimantan.

renewables.overview_html: Floating offshore wind moved from vision to concrete plan on 6 October, as GWEC and 50+ companies unveiled an industry action plan in Lisbon targeting floating wind FIDs before 2030. On M&A, Alight acquired a 2 GW, 40-project Swedish solar-plus-storage pipeline from Soltech on 1 October, bringing its Nordic pipeline past 5 GW; Inox Green completed the INR 550 crore payment for Wind World India’s 4.5 GW O&M business on 7 October, expanding its managed portfolio to 13.3 GWp. The macro backdrop: the IEA Electricity Mid-Year Update 2026 confirmed renewables overtook coal as the top global power source for the first time, with renewables’ share rising from 33% in 2025 toward 37% by 2027, led by 600 TWh of new solar PV.

items.headline: GWEC and 50+ Industry Leaders Launch Floating Wind Action Plan in Lisbon; Three Focus Areas: Cost Reduction, Finance/Insurance Access, Supply Chain Scale; First-Mover FIDs Targeted Before 2030
items.summary: The Global Wind Energy Council's Floating Wind Industry Accelerator (FWIA), established December 2025 and developed through ten months of industry consultations, unveiled its FWIA Action Statement for Accelerating Floating Wind on October 6, 2026 in Lisbon. More than 50 developers, manufacturers, suppliers, investors, insurers and technical experts endorsed the plan. Three principal areas for government-industry collaboration: (1) reducing the levelised cost of floating wind; (2) expanding access to finance and insurance while lowering cost of capital; and (3) scaling supply chains through infrastructure, standardisation and innovation. The initiative targets first-mover projects reaching final investment decisions before 2030, establishing conditions for wider industry expansion in the 2030s. Floating wind is critical to unlocking deep-water countries including Japan, Norway, the US West Coast and the Mediterranean where fixed-bottom foundations are not viable.

items.headline: Alight Acquires 2 GW Solar-Plus-Storage Development Pipeline from Soltech Energy Sweden; 40 Utility-Scale Projects in SE3/SE4 Zones; Nordic Pipeline Now Exceeds 5 GW
items.summary: Swedish solar developer Alight acquired a 40-project, ~2 GW solar PV development pipeline in southern Sweden from Soltech Energy Solutions on October 1, 2026, following approval from Sweden's Inspectorate of Strategic Products (ISP). Projects span SE3 and SE4 electricity price areas and include options for co-located battery energy storage at most sites. Following the transaction, Alight's Nordic solar and energy storage development pipeline exceeds 5 GW.

items.headline: Inox Green Completes INR 550 Crore Payment for Wind World India 4.5 GW O&M Business; Managed Portfolio Expands to 13.3 GWp; India’s Only Listed Renewable O&M Platform
items.summary: Inox Green Energy Services completed payment of INR 550 crore (including taxes, approximately US$65 million) on October 7, 2026 for Wind World India's (WWIL) 4.5 GW operations and maintenance business, via its subsidiary Vibhav Energy Private Limited (VEPL). The O&M portfolio services major clients including Tata Group, ReNew, Greenko, Apraava Energy and Hindustan Zinc. Following the transaction, Inox Green's total managed portfolio expands to approximately 13.3 GWp, consolidating its position as India's only listed company focused primarily on renewable energy O&M services.

items.headline: Spain Renewables Hit 50.9% of Power Mix in September 2026 — New Monthly Record; 52.7% Including Self-Consumption; Wind, Solar and Hydro Drive Record
items.summary: Spain's electricity grid operator REE confirmed renewable sources accounted for 50.9% of national electricity generation in September 2026 (52.7% including distributed self-consumption), a new monthly renewable share record driven by strong wind output and continued solar capacity additions since Spain crossed the 50 GW solar milestone in February 2026.

items.headline: Adani Green Energy Khavda BESS Expands to 6.63 GWh — World’s Largest Single-Location Battery Outside China; Over 50% of India’s Operational BESS at One Site
items.summary: Adani Green Energy expanded operational BESS capacity at Khavda, Gujarat from 3.55 GWh to 6.63 GWh, commissioning the new block in 10 months from construction start. Khavda now holds the world's largest operational single-location battery installation outside China, accounting for more than 50% of India's total operational BESS capacity of approximately 12.6 GWh.

items.headline: Australia: Synergy Proposes A$2 Billion Solar and Battery Addition at Warradarge Wind Farm in Western Australia; Among Largest Hybrid Renewable Projects in Southern Hemisphere
items.summary: Western Australian state-owned utility Synergy unveiled plans to develop a A$2 billion (~US$1.3 billion) co-located solar and battery storage project at the recently expanded Warradarge Wind Farm — currently the largest wind farm in Western Australia — creating one of Australia's largest hybrid renewable energy projects by leveraging existing transmission connection and site permits.

items.source: IEA / Renewable Energy Industry / Down to Earth
items.headline: IEA Electricity Mid-Year Update 2026: Renewables Overtake Coal as Top Global Power Source for First Time; 8% Generation Growth; Share Rising From 33% to 37% by 2027; Solar Adds 600 TWh; Demand +3.6%
items.summary: The IEA's Electricity Mid-Year Update 2026 confirmed that renewable energy sources are generating more electricity than coal-fired plants for the first time in history, making them the world's largest source of power generation. Global electricity consumption is expected to rise 3.6% in 2026, with renewable generation growing more than 8%, raising its share from 33% in 2025 toward 37% by 2027. Solar PV remains the largest contributor to supply growth, with generation forecast to increase by ~600 TWh in 2026 — matching the record annual expansion of 2025. Key growth drivers include electrification of industry, transport and heating, and expanding AI data centre demand.

science.overview_html: The Met Office and Alan Turing Institute published peer-reviewed research on FastNet, a graph neural network that embeds physical consistency constraints during training, addressing the sharp-fronts blurring endemic to existing AI weather models while matching or exceeding the Met Office Global Model on key metrics. A probabilistic extension of Microsoft’s Aurora, Xaurora converts Aurora into a generative ensemble system using stochastic interpolants at a fraction of the cost of training from scratch. And the Washington Post synthesises why AI models excel at hurricane track but consistently fail on intensity — sparse open-ocean data, chaotic attractor dynamics, and unresolved sub-mesoscale inner-core processes are the three root causes.

items.source: Met Office / Alan Turing Institute / Meteorological Technology International
items.headline: FastNet v1.0: Met Office and Turing Institute GNN Embeds Physical Consistency Constraints; Matches or Exceeds Met Office Global Model on Key Metrics; Validated Against Hurricane Ian and Storm Ciarán
items.meta: Met Office / Alan Turing Institute · arXiv:2509.17658 (physics.ao-ph) · Published October 2026
items.summary: Researchers at The Alan Turing Institute and Met Office published peer-reviewed research on FastNet v1.0, a graph neural network (GNN) architecture for global medium-range weather prediction that embeds physical consistency constraints during training — rather than as post-hoc corrections — producing forecasts that respect atmospheric dynamics. The model achieved accuracy comparable to the Met Office's Global Model, exceeding it on some metrics, and is computationally tens of thousands of times faster than full physics-based simulation. Validation included tests against Hurricane Ian (2022) and Storm Ciarán (2023), demonstrating more realistic storm core structures, improved pressure-wind relationships and higher peak wind speeds. FastNet addresses the sharp-fronts blurring that has been a persistent weakness of pure data-driven AI weather models.

items.source: VU Amsterdam / TU Delft / University of Amsterdam / EMS Annual Meeting 2026
items.headline: Xaurora: Probabilistic Generative Weather Forecasting Using Stochastic Interpolants on Aurora Foundation Model; Competitive with DLWP Ensembles at Fraction of Training Cost; arXiv Preprint
items.meta: Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, TU Delft, University of Amsterdam · EMS Annual Meeting 2026 · arXiv preprint (October 2026)
items.summary: Xaurora, presented at the EMS Annual Meeting 2026 by researchers from Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, Delft University of Technology, and the University of Amsterdam, uses the stochastic interpolant framework to convert Microsoft's Aurora (1.3 billion-parameter Earth system foundation model) into a fully generative ensemble forecast system. The key approach fine-tunes Aurora as a drift prediction model using low-rank adaptation (LoRA), making the conversion computationally inexpensive compared to training probabilistic DLWP from scratch. Results show competitive performance against state-of-the-art NWP ensembles and other data-driven approaches across a range of weather and climate modelling tasks. The principal contribution is a practical pathway for converting any large pre-trained deterministic weather foundation model into a stochastic ensemble system.

items.source: Washington Post / CBC / Yale Climate Connections
items.headline: Why AI Models Excel at Hurricane Track but Fail at Intensity: Sparse Ocean Observations, Chaotic Attractor Dynamics and Unresolved Inner-Core Processes Explain the Gap
items.summary: A Washington Post investigation synthesises why AI weather models — despite achieving track forecast skill rivalling or exceeding traditional NWP — consistently underperform at predicting hurricane intensification. Three root causes: (1) open-ocean observations are far sparser than near-coastal measurements, creating uneven training data distributions; (2) hurricane intensity operates within a chaotic attractor where minor initial-condition perturbations rapidly amplify regardless of data quality; and (3) rapid intensification is driven by sub-mesoscale inner-core ocean–atmosphere interactions below the spatial resolution of global training datasets. Some AI models showed virtually no intensity skill while performing well on track. The article contrasts this with specialised intensity models (e.g. HFIP consensus products) that explicitly target inner-core scales.

items.headline: Varda-single-1.0 (arXiv:2610.01835): First Kilometre-Scale Data-Driven Weather Forecast System Over Alpine Topography; Competitive with ICON-CH1-EPS to +33 h, Outperforms ICON-CH2-EPS to +120 h
items.meta: Alberto Pennino et al. · arXiv:2610.01835 (physics.ao-ph, cs.LG) · Submitted 1 October 2026
items.summary: Varda-single-1.0 is the first medium-range data-driven weather prediction system targeting 1 km resolution over the Swiss Alps. The architecture pairs a 6-hourly autoregressive global model at 31 km with a temporal downscaler reconstructing hourly 1 km forecasts. Trained on ERA5 pre-training, then 20-year kilometre-scale regional reanalysis fine-tuning, then operational km-scale analysis final fine-tuning, Varda-single is competitive with ICON-CH1-EPS control to +33 h and outperforms ICON-CH2-EPS control to +120 h. Weaknesses include underestimation of local wind maxima and overly smooth convective precipitation. Built on the Anemoi framework, it represents a significant step toward replacing LAM NWP in complex terrain with purely data-driven systems.

items.headline: ClimateBench v2.0 (arXiv:2610.04558): Three-Tier Probabilistic Benchmarking Protocol for Climate Models; Tier I–III from Energy Conservation to Paleoclimate Out-of-Distribution; CRPS Primary Score; All Code Public
items.meta: Duncan Watson-Parris et al. · arXiv:2610.04558 (physics.ao-ph, cs.LG) · Submitted 3 October 2026
items.summary: ClimateBench v2.0 establishes a standardized multi-tier evaluation protocol allowing physics-based, data-driven and hybrid climate models to be compared on equal terms. Tier I tests physical credibility via energy conservation, co-variability and basic forced responses. Tier II scores models against post-2015 observations using fair Continuous Ranked Probability Score (CRPS) as the primary metric. Tier III evaluates out-of-distribution generalization through paleoclimate simulations covering the Last Interglacial, Last Glacial Maximum and Mid-Holocene. All evaluation code, observational data and benchmarks are publicly available.

items.headline: Post-Training Quantization of Autoregressive Weather Models (arXiv:2610.02511): 8-Bit PTQ Retains Near-Full Skill for DLWP and FourCastNet; Path to Edge Deployment on Drones and Satellites
items.meta: Bhattacharya, Bhattacharya, Jablonowski · arXiv:2610.02511 (cs.LG, physics.ao-ph) · Submitted 1 October 2026
items.summary: Bhattacharya et al. apply post-training quantization (PTQ) to DLWP and FourCastNet, compressing from 32-bit to 8-bit precision using only a small calibration dataset with no access to the original training pipeline. 8-bit quantization retains near-full forecast skill; degradation emerges primarily at 4-bit and below. The practical implication: production MLWP models could be compressed for deployment on edge hardware — satellites, drones, autonomous balloons — enabling real-time in-situ inference for nowcasting and data assimilation in resource-constrained environments.

items.headline: Climate-Driven Atmospheric Angular Momentum Changes Measurably Lengthening Earth’s Day; Projected to Reach 10–18% of Tidal Friction by 2100; Current Rate Unprecedented in 3.6 Million Years
items.summary: New research demonstrates that global warming-driven reorganisation of atmospheric circulation is measurably influencing Earth's rotational dynamics. High-emissions simulations project that by 2100, the atmospheric contribution to day-length increase will reach 10–18% of the long-term tidal friction trend. Under very high emissions, climate-driven day lengthening could reach 2.62 ms per century — potentially overtaking the Moon's tidal influence (~2.4 ms/century). The current measured rate of 1.33 ms/century is described as unprecedented in the past 3.6 million years.

items.headline: Global Heat Stress Intensification: Up to 50 Additional Heat Stress Days Per Year in Most-Impacted Regions; Hottest Nights Warming Faster Than Days (0.32 vs. 0.27°C/Decade); Compound Events Rising Sharply
items.meta: Multiple authors · Nature Climate Change Vol. 16, pp. 989–996 (2026) · doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02670-5
items.summary: A Nature Climate Change study found heat stress days increased by up to 50 per year in the most-impacted regions (parts of South Asia, sub-Saharan Africa and the Arabian Peninsula). Tropical nights are warming faster than the hottest days (0.32°C vs. 0.27°C per decade) — with serious implications for human thermal recovery during heatwaves. Compound daytime–nighttime events increased sharply in frequency since the 2000s. Low- and middle-income countries face disproportionate exposure even as total global heat stress expands.

items.title: Inox Green Energy Services Completes INR 550 Crore Payment for Wind World India’s 4.5 GW O&M Business; Managed Portfolio Expands to 13.3 GWp; India’s Only Listed Renewable O&M Specialist
items.body_html: Inox Green Energy Services completed the INR 550 crore (~US$65M) payment for Wind World India’s (WWIL) 4.5 GW operations and maintenance business on 7 October 2026, executed via subsidiary Vibhav Energy Private Limited following NCLT approval. The acquired O&M portfolio services clients including Tata Group, ReNew Power, Greenko Group, Apraava Energy and Hindustan Zinc across Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh. This is a distinct transaction from Inox Clean Energy’s earlier $627.5M acquisition of Vena Energy India’s 6 GW generation portfolio. Following both transactions, the broader Inox Group now operates India’s largest independent renewable O&M platform at 13.3 GWp — and Inox Green remains the country’s only listed company focused primarily on renewable O&M services as a standalone business model.

items.title: Enel Green Power Closes Acquisition of 270 MW US Solar Portfolio for $140 Million; Seven Plants Across Virginia, North and South Carolina; ~$20M Annual EBITDA Contribution
items.body_html: Enel Green Power closed the acquisition of seven operational photovoltaic plants in the United States with an aggregate installed capacity of ~270 MW on October 6, 2026, at a total consideration of approximately $140 million. The deal was originally signed in May 2026, with closing subject to FERC and antitrust approvals. The portfolio spans Virginia (two projects, over 120 MW), North Carolina (one project, over 90 MW), and South Carolina (four projects, ~50 MW), adding an estimated $20 million annually to Enel’s consolidated EBITDA. The acquisition expands Enel’s US renewable footprint ahead of IRA investment tax credit expirations.

items.title: KPI Green Energy Signs Binding Offer to Acquire 507.9 MW of Operational Gujarat Wind Capacity from Alfanar Group for INR 24.1 Billion (~US$288M); Largest Operational Wind M&A Deal in India This Year; Close Expected February 2027
items.body_html: KPI Green Energy signed a binding offer on October 5, 2026 to acquire 507.9 MW of operational wind projects in Gujarat from Saudi-backed Alfanar Group for an enterprise value of approximately INR 24.1 billion (US$288 million). The portfolio comprises the Bhuj-1 (301.4 MW, Alfanar Energy) and Bhuj-2 (206.5 MW, Netra Wind Private Limited) projects in the high-resource Kutch wind corridor. Both projects hold long-term PPAs with SECI with a capacity-weighted remaining life of 21 years, providing strong contracted revenue certainty. Enterprise value translates to approximately INR 48 million per MW — market-consistent for operating Indian wind assets with long-dated SECI offtake. Transaction expected to close February 2027, pending regulatory approvals.

items.title: Inox Clean Energy Completes $627.5M Acquisition of Vena Energy India’s 6 GW Renewable Portfolio; Operating Capacity Expands to 4 GW; Total Pipeline Exceeds 12 GW; GIP (BlackRock) Exits India
items.body_html: Inox Clean Energy completed the acquisition of Vena Energy India for INR 60 billion (US$627.5 million), finalising a deal originally announced June 2026. The portfolio from BlackRock-owned Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) comprises 1.2 GW of operational assets, 1.8 GW at advanced development stage, and 3 GW of early-pipeline projects across solar, wind and hybrid. Following the transaction, Inox Clean Energy’s operating portfolio expands to ~4 GW while its total development pipeline exceeds 12 GW. The deal marks GIP’s full exit from the Indian renewable energy market.

items.title: Euler ILS Partners Signs Multi-Year Catastrophe Risk Analytics Agreement with Moody’s; Access to Natural Catastrophe and Cyber Risk Models, Intelligent Risk Platform; Cat Bond Issuance Hits Record $65.6 Billion Outstanding
items.body_html: Euler ILS Partners, the specialist Swiss ILS investment manager, signed a multi-year agreement on September 29, 2026 with Moody’s to utilise its catastrophe risk models, analytics and exposure datasets via the Moody’s Intelligent Risk Platform™, granting access to both natural catastrophe and cyber risk models and specialised peril and exposure datasets to inform ILS investment decisions. The deal follows Moody’s launch of Risk InvestorIQ on September 18, a dedicated cat risk analytics and portfolio management application for ILS professionals. The ILS market reached a record $65.6 billion in cat bond issuance outstanding by mid-2026, with H1 2026 new issuance of almost $18 billion also hitting a new high.
